title: Deny Beats the Catch-All
summary: A catch-all allows almost everything. An Always Deny rule on one action still shuts that door.
lesson: An exact rule always wins over the catch-all. Give it the Always Deny policy to close one door, and remember that a permissive catch-all covers everything else: the Safe settings, and even burning ETH to the zero address.

rules.note: Allows every CALL without its own rule

steps.label: Pay Erin 200 USDC
steps.note: USDC transfers have no rule of their own, so the catch-all allows them.

steps.label: Approve Mallory to spend 1000 USDC
steps.note: The exact rule is found first, so the catch-all is never asked.

steps.label: Revoke Mallory's approval
steps.note: Always Deny does not read the call. Even setting an approval to zero is refused.

steps.label: Add Mallory as an owner
steps.note: Careful: the catch-all also covers the Safe settings. Nothing stops two owners from adding Mallory.

steps.label: Send 1 ETH to the zero address
steps.note: The zero address has no rule of its own, and a plain transfer to it has the same key as the catch-all rule. So the permissive catch-all also lets the Safe burn ETH by sending it to the zero address.
